Possibly borrowed from Polish produkować. Ultimately from Latin prōdūcō + -ува́ти (-uváty).

parole.significato: ray, beam (beam of light or radiation)

parole.significato: recommendation, reference, character reference (commendation or endorsement of a person)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Polish rekomendacja, from Medieval Latin recommendātiō. Compare Russian рекоменда́ция (rekomendácija), Belarusian рэкаменда́цыя (rekamjendácyja).
Borrowed from Polish rekrut or Russian ре́крут (rékrut).
Borrowed from Polish rzetelny.

parole.significato: rest, remainder (that which is left over)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Polish reszta.

Borrowed from Polish ryzyko, from German Risiko, from Italian risco (“risk”) (modern Italian rischio). Compare Russian риск (risk), Belarusian ры́зыка (rýzyka).

parole.significato: a pipe or trough intended for drainage of water; gutter, leader, or eavestrough
parole.testo: From Polish rynwa, a dialectal form of rynna, from Middle High German rinne.
Borrowed from Polish rynek.

parole.significato: stroke, line (often metaphorically as the fundamental way something is constructed)

parole.significato: to corrupt, to debauch, to deprave, to pervert (erode the moral adherence of; influence someone to behave badly)

Borrowed from Polish sejm. Doublet of сойм (sojm), the inherited form.

parole.significato: session (meeting of a council, court, school, or legislative body to conduct its business)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Polish sesja, from Latin sessiō, from sedeō (“to sit”). Compare Russian се́ссия (séssija).

parole.significato: sympathy (favorable attitude; affinity, association or mutual relationship)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Polish sympatia, from Latin sympathīa, from Ancient Greek συμπάθεια (sumpátheia). Compare Russian симпа́тия (simpátija), Belarusian сімпа́тыя (simpátyja).

parole.significato: to scan (to read or mark so as to show a specific metre)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Polish skandować, from German skandieren, from French scander, from Late Latin scandō, with -ува́ти (-uváty) ending. Compare Russian сканди́ровать (skandírovatʹ), Belarusian скандава́ць (skandavácʹ).

parole.significato: good, right, pertinent, opportune (appropriate or useful for a certain purpose at a given moment)

parole.significato: treat, goody, sunket (small amount of something good to eat)

parole.significato: back, the rear of the torso

parole.significato: to like (the person who likes takes the dative case), to be to the liking of, to please

Borrowed from Polish stateczny, from Old Polish stateczny, from Proto-Slavic *statъčьnъ.

parole.significato: wheelwright (a person who builds and repairs wheels, especially wooden spoked ones)

parole.significato: to hold back (to contain, to stop)

parole.significato: the end of something, such as working time (used with a preposition)

parole.significato: sage (any plant in the genus Salvia)

parole.significato: shawl (a square piece of cloth worn as a covering for the head, neck, and shoulders)

parole.significato: scalepan, scale (either of the pans, trays, or dishes of a balance or scales)

parole.significato: szlachta (nobility in Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, including Belarus and Northern Ukraine)

parole.significato: to grind (to remove material by rubbing with an abrasive surface)

parole.significato: wallpaper (decorative paper-like material used to cover the inner walls of buildings)

parole.significato: piece (single item belonging to a class of similar items)

parole.significato: button (knob or small disc serving as a fastener)
parole.testo: From Polish guzik or from ґудз (gudz, “button (rare)”) + -ик (-yk).
Borrowed from Polish gorzelnia.
